newsitem.title: GERMANY: Premiere gets court to block Kirch TV competition.
newsitem.headline: Premiere gets court to block Kirch TV competition.

text.p: Pay-TV broadcaster Premiere said it had won a court injunction against media mogul Leo Kirch, preventing his DF1 digital channel from directly competing with it by broadcasting big-name films.
DF1 said it would contest the ruling, but a spokesman there declined further comment. Kirch also owns 25 percent of Premiere, but Bertelsmann AG, with a 37.5 percent stake, has control of management.
Bertelsmann and Kirch have been locked for more than a year in a battle over the future direction of Premiere.
Kirch, who has a massive arsenal of rights to Hollywood feature films, wants to broadcast these on his new DF1 digital channel as pay-per-view rather than on Premiere.
Bertelsmann wants to make sure that Kirch's films are first shown on Premiere, which until July was Germany's only pay TV channel and has some 1.2 million subscribers.
Canal Plus of France, Europe's biggest pay TV broadcaster, also holds 37.5 percent of Premiere and has so far stood by Bertelsmann in the dispute with Kirch.
At issue is Cinedom, the pay-per-view channel on Kirch's DF1 digital platform of 17 channels. Cinedom hopes to broadcast first-run feature films for around six marks per film.

In the past six months, Kirch is believed to have spent some $5 billion to obtain digital pay TV rights from all of the major studios in Hollywood, pushing Bertelsmann out of the race for leadership in digital pay TV in Germany.
But Bertelsmann and Kirch have reached a stalemate.
While Kirch has the Hollywood programming, his DF1 has lagged well behind expectations since its July launch. At the same time Premiere has seen a boom in new subscriptions.
Most new subscribers to Premiere have signed on for its live broadcasts of German first division soccer, to which Bertelsmann holds the rights for the next two years.
But the battle over movies could inflict "life-threatening damages" on Premiere, the broadcaster's managing director Bernd Kundrun said.
